title: Upper endoscopy for children
what: The doctor looks at your child's food pipe, stomach, and the start of the small bowel with a thin, flexible tube with a camera, passed through the mouth.
why: For frequent belly pain, vomiting, possible gastritis or an ulcer, a swallowed object, bleeding, or poor weight gain.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 5 to 15 minutes; after sedation, about an hour of observation; the report usually right away
tell_doctor: Heart or lung disease, or seizures
If your child recently had a cold
If your child had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 hours and no drinks for 2 hours. For babies, the times may be shorter. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Sedation
prepare.text: Children usually have the test while asleep. The anesthesiologist will explain in advance how it works.

prepare.title: Talk
prepare.text: Explain to your child in simple words: the doctor will look at the tummy with a tiny camera while they sleep.

bring: A change of clothes and water for after
steps: Your child is weighed, and the anesthesiologist talks with them
Usually one parent stays with the child while they fall asleep
Your child falls asleep through a mask or with medicine into a vein
The doctor passes a thin tube through the mouth
The food pipe, stomach, and bowel are checked, and a small tissue sample is taken if needed
Your child wakes up in the recovery room, and you are called in
feel: While asleep, your child feels nothing
Afterward, your child may be sleepy or fussy, and the throat may feel scratchy
after: Your child can usually drink and eat after 1 to 2 hours. Start with water
Your child may be drowsy until evening. That is normal
The report usually right away, biopsy results in 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Vomiting blood or black stools: call emergency services
Severe pain in the belly or chest, or trouble breathing: call emergency services
A high fever in the first 24 hours: tell your doctor

faq.q: Can I stay with my child?
faq.a: Usually a parent stays while the child falls asleep and is nearby when they wake up. Ask the clinic about its rules.

faq.q: Can it be done without anesthesia?
faq.a: Teens sometimes have it with a throat spray while awake. Young children are usually asleep.

reminders.text: Your child's upper endoscopy is tomorrow. Food and drinks only until the times your clinic gave you. Bring a toy.
